note: Merged/ready real issue proposing a new audit skill for the instruction corpus itself; today's A4 autonomous_completion criterion and A4.5 verifiability check both false-positive on its own meta/self-referential "instruction corpus" prose (known lexical-gate boundary gap).
title: Introduce a repo-local semantic spec-audit skill for the instruction corpus
body:
Blocked by #1592
Blocked by #1593

Part of the `soloscrum-spec-quality-adoption` roadmap (#1598).

## Background

`scripts/audit-docs.mjs` mechanically checks byte-level drift (sync
pairs, budgets, config-vs-instruction agreement) but cannot detect
**semantic** drift: prose that contradicts a sibling file, leaked
session context, passages not completable from a cold read, or wording
that stalls an autonomous step. Real incidents exist — the #1439 and
#1522 same-file semantic collision was caught only by post-ship
advisory review. `mew-ton/soloscrum` (evaluated 2026-07-22) formalizes
exactly this audit as four rule sets — R1 leaked session context, R2
cross-file contradictions over a closed concept index, R3 fresh-memory
completability, R4 automation blockers — run as N parallel LLM passes
aggregated by union with dedup (`Appeared in: K/N` is informational;
quorum filtering is explicitly an anti-pattern because it conflates
sampling variance with finding validity), read-only, with fixes routed
back through the normal flow.

Per maintainer decision (2026-07-22 hearing), this lands
**dogfood-only**: repo-local under `.claude/`, not distributed, with a
built-in recurring promotion checkpoint that keeps asking whether to
promote it to distributed status.

Dependency justification: R4's autonomy cross-check takes the
reversible/irreversible classification table (#1592) as its closed
source of truth, and R2's concept index seeds from the
concept-ownership matrix (#1593); shipping the audit before its
reference docs would force both rule sets to re-derive their authority
from prose on every run.

## Proposed change

- Add `.claude/skills/idd-spec-audit/SKILL.md` plus
  `.claude/skills/idd-spec-audit/references/report-template.md`
  defining:
  - **Scope**: `.github/instructions/**/*.md` (including `lite/`),
    `skills/issue-authoring/**/*.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, and
    `.github/copilot-instructions.md`. Excluded: `.claude/**` (the
    audit never audits itself), `docs/**` (summary docs rely on
    referenced files by design), and generated copies already covered
    by their canonical source via sync pairs.
  - **Rule sets** adapted from soloscrum to IDD:
    - R1 — leaked session context (time-relative phrasing without an
      absolute anchor, first-person session voice, edit narration,
      workaround prose without a tracking link);
    - R2 — cross-file contradictions over a **closed v1 concept
      index**, seeded with: claim-marker and activation-nonce
      semantics; advisory-convergence satisfaction; merge-gate order
      (F2/F2.5/F3); the "ready = absence of `status:*` labels"
      definition; phase-digest rules; forced-handoff marker semantics;
      the suitability/effort footer contracts — finalized against the
      #1593 matrix. Expanding the index is a spec change, not an
      in-audit decision;
    - R3 — fresh-memory completability (unresolved references, implied
      prerequisites, missing exit conditions, half-named cross-refs);
    - R4 — automation blockers, cross-checked against the #1592
      classification: a "confirm with the user" instruction on a
      transition classified reversible is a finding; the same phrase on
      an irreversible transition is expected and never flagged.
  - **Execution**: N parallel read-only passes (default `3`,
    adjustable via a `--passes N`-style argument), aggregated by union
    with overlap-based dedup and an `Appeared in: K/N` annotation per
    finding; no quorum filter. The audit never edits files and never
    opens, closes, or labels issues — findings route through the
    normal issue-authoring flow.
  - **Promotion checkpoint (maintainer-requested)**: the skill's final
    step, after emitting the report, reminds the maintainer that the
    audit is dogfood-only and asks whether to decide now on promoting
    it to distributed status. The checkpoint text itself states that
    when promotion is adopted, removing this checkpoint section is part
    of the promotion change.
- Verify the new repo-local, non-generated `.claude/skills/`
  directory does not trip `audit-docs` or lint rules; if a mechanical
  check flags the new path, add the narrowest possible exemption and
  record why.
- Run the audit once end-to-end and attach the produced report to the
  PR description as execution evidence (any pass count is acceptable
  for the dry run).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `SKILL.md` and the report template exist under
      `.claude/skills/idd-spec-audit/` and the skill is discoverable by
      Claude Code in this repository.
- [ ] The four rule sets, the closed v1 concept index, the `.claude/**`
      self-exclusion, and the read-only/no-issue-mutation constraints
      are all stated in the skill.
- [ ] Default 3 passes with argument-adjustable pass count and
      union/no-quorum aggregation are specified.
- [ ] The promotion checkpoint, including its self-removal-on-adoption
      clause, is the skill's final step.
- [ ] A dry-run report is attached to the PR description.
- [ ] `node scripts/audit-docs.mjs --check` and the repository lint
      pass.
